introduction: Two observatories contribute to this composite view of the Crab Nebula, a supernova remnant in the Milky Way.
observe: Look for structures that appear to belong to different visual layers.
Compare this restrained combination with the five-observatory Crab view later in the Trail.
explanation: The record combines observations from the Herschel Space Observatory and the Hubble Space Telescope rather than presenting a single exposure.
colorMethod: The source identifies the image as a Herschel–Hubble composite. Its colors should be read as a combined scientific view, not assumed to be a naked-eye scene.
whyItMatters: Combining instruments can place different physical structures into one frame while preserving their relationship in space.
